table leave_policies | fields: id, policy_name, leave_type, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: leave_type: filtering policies by leave type category; is_active: filtering active policies for assignment and validation

table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_policy_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_policy_id -> leave_policies.id; approved_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: lookups for employee leave history and dashboard; status: filtering by status (SUBMITTED for manager queues, APPROVED/REJECTED for reporting); leave_policy_id: filtering by leave type; start_date, end_date: date-range queries for calendar views and overlap detection; approved_by: manager approval history lookups

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, leave_policy_id, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, fiscal_year, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_policy_id -> leave_policies.id | indexes: employee_id: lookups for employee balance dashboard; leave_policy_id: filtering balances by policy type; fiscal_year: filtering balances by fiscal year; employee_id, leave_policy_id, fiscal_year: unique constraint enforcement for one balance per employee-policy-year

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: performed_by -> employees.id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: lookups for audit trail of a specific entity; performed_by: audit lookups by actor; performed_at: time-range audit queries; action: filtering by action type

data_notes: All tables use UUID primary keys (id). Timestamps (created_at, updated_at) follow the BaseEntity convention from DOMAIN.md. The leave_requests.status field uses the LeaveStatus enum values: DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED. The leave_balances table enforces a unique constraint on (employee_id, leave_policy_id, fiscal_year) — one balance row per employee-policy-year. The audit_logs table supports GP-002: every state-changing operation writes an audit record. The employees table is defined here as a dependency for FK relationships; its full ownership belongs to the employee module. leave_policies is defined here as a dependency; its full ownership belongs to the policy module.

open_questions.question: How are leave days counted from start_date and end_date? Are both dates inclusive? Are weekends and/or public holidays excluded from the count?
open_questions.impact: This is BINDING — it determines the used_days value deducted from leave_balances.remaining_days on approval, affects overlap detection logic, and must be consistent across all call sites (approval, balance display, reporting).
candidate_options: Calendar days inclusive of both start and end (endDate - startDate + 1)
Calendar days exclusive of end date (endDate - startDate)
Business days only (exclude weekends and public holidays via a holiday calendar)

open_questions.question: What defines the fiscal_year boundary for leave balances? Is it a calendar year, a company-configured fiscal year, or an employee-specific anniversary year?
open_questions.impact: BINDING — determines which balance row is used when approving a leave request and when displaying remaining balances. Affects balance lookup queries, accrual scheduling, and year-end carryover logic across all modules.

transaction_contract: Repository methods that must join a caller's transaction take an optional PoolClient parameter (defaulting to the shared pool when omitted). The calling service owns the unit of work: it acquires a client from the pool, calls BEGIN, passes the client to each participating repository method, then calls COMMIT or ROLLBACK. Specifically: ILeaveRequestRepository.updateStatus and ILeaveBalanceRepository.updateUsedDays/upsert accept an optional client parameter. The leave approval service method acquires a client, begins a transaction, calls updateStatus + updateUsedDays with the client, and commits — ensuring the status change and balance deduction are atomic.
